claim.pdf_says: In the 4.3.2 OPEN general format a drawn box encloses both the INPUT phrase's bracket [REVERSED / WITH NO REWIND] and the OUTPUT phrase's [WITH NO REWIND] (one box spanning the two lines), the same box notation that encloses 'EXTEND {file-name-4} ...'.
claim.why_it_matters: The transcription keeps the box marker (║) around the EXTEND line but drops the box around the REVERSED / WITH NO REWIND bracket and the OUTPUT [WITH NO REWIND] bracket, so the figure no longer shows that these phrases are boxed (higher-level/obsolete-marked) elements. Syntax itself (brackets, braces, ellipses, underlining) is otherwise faithful.

verdict.reasoning: On the 300 dpi render of page 413 (VII-39), section 4.3.2 shows one drawn rectangle. It starts above the REVERSED / WITH NO REWIND bracket on the INPUT line and ends below [WITH NO REWIND] on the OUTPUT line, so it encloses both brackets. A separate rectangle encloses 'EXTEND {file-name-4} ...'. In page-413.md the EXTEND line keeps its ║ ... ║ box markers. The INPUT bracket (┌ REVERSED ┐ / └ WITH NO REWIND ┘) and the OUTPUT '[ WITH NO REWIND ]' carry no box marker. In the 1985 text a box marks higher-level or obsolete material; 4.3.1 and SR1 box the REVERSED phrase in exactly that way. The transcription therefore loses the information that the REVERSED and NO REWIND phrases are boxed elements. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
